Salutations to Rāma, to Rāma, to Rāma, to the strong one, salutations!

Salutations to the Buddha, the pure one, the compassionate one, salutations, salutations!
Salutations be to you, O Kalki! Salutations to you of manifold forms!

To Nārāyaṇa, to Kṛṣṇa, to Govinda, and to the wielder of the Śārṅga bow,
to Dāmodara, to the God, to the God of gods, salutations to you!

To Hṛṣīkeśa, to the tranquil one, to the one whose foot spans the sky, salutations!
Salutations be to the Lord of Padmā! Salutations to you with lotus-eyes!

Salutations to you, Ananta! Salutations to the one whose hand holds the mace!
To you whose banner bears Garuḍa, salutations to you, discus in hand!

Salutations to you, lotus in hand! To Acyuta, salutations, salutations!
Salutations to you, enemy of the Daityas, bestower of all desires!

To Mādhava, to the Lord of gods, to Viṣṇu, the Supreme Self,
to the diadem-wearer, to the earring-wearer, salutations ever be to Hari!

Salutations to you, Blessed Lord; his vehicle is named Garuḍa—
with the mantra: "Salutations to Garuḍa," the discerning one [worships it].

Salutations to the conch, to the discus, and to the mace, salutations, salutations!
Salutations to the lotus, to the sword, to Nandaka, salutations, salutations!'
Having thus worshipped the lord of gods along with his wife, along with his mount, / and along with his weapon, the wise person should then repeat the eight-syllable mantra:

Then, having recited the eight-syllable mantra with his own devotion, the wise one
should then present varied and excellent food-offerings to Govinda,

and incense, a lamp, and betel to Viṣṇu, the God of gods.
The Vaiṣṇava person should present other offerings as well.

The one who gives incense scented with sandalwood and agallochum to Murāri, O best of Brahmins,
his desire is swiftly accomplished.

The one who gives incense scented with clarified butter to Hari, O Brahmin,
freed from millions of sins, would go to Viṣṇu's abode.

The one who gives incense scented with bdellium to Nārāyaṇa,
he goes to the supreme abode, which is difficult even for the gods to attain.

The one who offers a lamp with clarified butter, or with sesame oil,
Keśava removes all of his sin in the twinkling of an eye.

The one who gives betel scented with camphor to the wielder of the discus,
for him, O best of Brahmins, liberation is achieved, O Jaimini.

The one who offers betel combined with catechu,
having enjoyed all pleasures here, goes in the end to the abode of Hari.

Having offered betel furnished with liquorice and sweet fennel, and with nutmeg and other [spices], to Hari,
a mortal attains heaven.

Having placed water in a conch, a Vaiṣṇava person should perform circumambulation of Viṣṇu
with the mantra about to be spoken, O Jaimini:
"O Janārdana, friend of the world, protector of those who have come for refuge, / grant me, O Lord, to be a servant of the servant of a servant of your servant."

The fruit of merit of the one who circumambulates Nārāyaṇa with this mantra,
I shall state in brief; listen, O Jaimini.

Whatever sins there are, such as the slaying of a Brahmin, and whatever great [crimes],
all of them are destroyed at each step of the circumambulation.

As many steps as a man takes with devotion in circumambulating Viṣṇu,
for that many thousands of kalpas he rejoices with Viṣṇu.

As many steps as one walks slowly in circumambulating Hari,
at every step a mortal attains the fruit of a horse sacrifice.

Whatever fruit there may be from circumambulating the whole world,
from circumambulating Hari the fruit is ten million times greater than that.

And the one who circumambulates his own body in the presence of Nārāyaṇa,
he too attains that fruit; what need is there of many other words?

The wise man should not cross the soma-channel in circumambulating Śambhu;
when one crosses it, O Brahmin, that worship becomes fruitless.

The one who circles Hari once in the manner of circumambulation,
in birth after birth, O best of Brahmins, he certainly becomes a universal monarch.

The one who performs circumambulation of Viṣṇu twice, O Brahmin,
attains the state of Indra in three days; of this there is no doubt.

The person who performs circumambulation of Viṣṇu twice,
freed from all sins, would enter the body of Mādhava.
One should wave a conch filled with water over Keśava, O Jaimini; / in the end, having gone to the abode of the gods, he will be praised by the deities.

The one who bows down seven times to Keśava like a staff upon the ground,
the sin resting in his body is reduced to ashes that very moment.

The one who bows down to Janārdana, placing joined palms on his head,
to him Viṣṇu, the Lord of Lakṣmī, gives the supreme abode.

Of mortals who bow down to Hari, casting all limbs upon the ground,
listen, O Brahmin-sage, as I declare the power of merit:

as long as the body of mortals is adorned with dust of the earth,
for that many thousands of kalpas they remain in Hari's presence.

Then the flower-remains of Keśava are given to the Vaiṣṇavas.
I shall declare those Vaiṣṇavas; listen, O best of men, Jaimini:
Śuka, Sūta, and also Vyāsa, Nārada, the sage Kapila, / Prahlāda and Ambarīṣa, and also Akrūra and Uddhava—

Vibhīṣaṇa, Hanūmat, and likewise other Vaiṣṇavas as well;
may they receive the flower-remains of Vāsudeva that fulfill all desires.'
Having spoken thus, the Vaiṣṇava should place the remnant of Viṣṇu's offering upon the ground; / then, indeed, he himself takes the remnant of Hari's offering with devotion.
Upon whose head the excellent withered offering of Hari is seen, / he should be known, O best of brahmins, as none other than Hari Himself.
Viṣṇu's food offering is hard to attain, and the withered flower offering destroys sin; / all the gods receive it, so what to say of human beings?
O Jaimini, the Vaiṣṇava who smells a tulasī leaf, / all the sin residing within his body is destroyed.
The fragrance of a tulasī leaf that enters a person's nose / causes misfortunes residing in his body to perish instantly.
He who rejoices having smelled the fragrance of a tulasī leaf, / in his abode there will be everlasting bliss, O best of brahmins.
Having praised the Lord of the universe, the beloved of Kamalā, Acyuta, with hymns, / with joined palms the wise man should then utter this mantra:
'O Nārāyaṇa whose form is the universe, go to Your abode, O Lord of the universe; / go, O God, to Your own place, and be pleased at all times.
This worship of You that has been performed by me according to my ability, / O Lord of gods, O Lord of the universe, let it be flawless by Your grace, O You whose self is the universe!'
Then the wise man should take with devotional disposition the foot-water / of Mahāviṣṇu, the Supreme Self, which destroys all sins.
He who carries even a single drop of the auspicious foot-water of Viṣṇu / has bathed in all holy places; O Jaimini, the truth is spoken.
If one touches the water from Viṣṇu's feet, the fruit of bathing in the Gaṅgā arises, / since the water of the Gaṅgā, O brāhmaṇa, is the water from Viṣṇu's feet.
There is no untimely death, nor is there fear of disease, / for one who touches the foot-water of great-souled Keśava.
For the destruction of sins and diseases, the water of Viṣṇu's feet is the medicine; / even sinful men should drink it every day.
The Vaiṣṇava person who drinks the water from Viṣṇu's feet, O brāhmaṇa, / the sin residing in his body is destroyed in an instant.
Just as what resides in the body of an embodied being is completely destroyed by medicine, / in the same way is all sin [destroyed] by the water of Viṣṇu's feet.
The pure water from Viṣṇu's feet accompanied by a tulasī leaf— / he who carries it on his head, O brāhmaṇa, I shall tell his merit:
freed from sins such as killing a brāhmaṇa, assuming the form of Viṣṇu, / going at the end to Viṣṇu's realm, he rejoices together with Viṣṇu.
Whatever fruit arises from giving gold equivalent to Mount Meru, / touching the water from Viṣṇu's feet produces a greater fruit than that.
Whatever fruit is attained by people through the gift of ten million horses, / whatever fruit one obtains by giving the earth of seven continents to brāhmaṇas,
that fruit a mortal obtains touching the water from Viṣṇu's feet. / Whatever fruit arises from performing a thousand horse sacrifices,
touching the water from Viṣṇu's feet produces a greater fruit than that. / Whatever merit is celebrated from the gift of a hundred oblong ponds,
touching the foot-water one obtains merit even greater than that. / What is the use of saying much here? It is stated briefly by me:
From the contact with the water of Viṣṇu's feet, a man becomes liberated. / Again and again, O best of brāhmaṇas, it is firmly declared by me:
touching the water from Hari's feet, one does not obtain birth again. / He who [eats] the remainder of food offered to Viṣṇu, which destroys all sins,
who eats it with devotional disposition, goes to the supreme abode. / One who eats the hard-to-attain food offered to Viṣṇu, O best of the twice-born,
sins, even beginning with the murder of a brāhmaṇa, abandon his body. / For him who eats the food offered to Hari, [liberation] becomes subservient like a maidservant.
The realm of liberation, O best of gods, is difficult to attain even by deities; / having worshipped the beloved of Kamalā, not abandoning even a little food-offering,
Viṣṇu leads him without delay to his own form. / What excellence of the food-offering of Mahāviṣṇu shall I tell?
"Eating which even Keśava becomes submissive, O chief of the twice-born; / by this rule, O twice-born, each month [one should worship] Janārdana."
whoever performs the worship of the lord of Kamalā, even if devoid of formal rules, / with devotional disposition, he too becomes dear to Keśava.
Whatever fruit one who knows the rules obtains by worshipping Viṣṇu according to the rules, / according to the prescribed rule, O brāhmaṇa, with abundant food-offerings, O lord,
even when worshipped he is not pleased if devotion is not present. / Whatever devotion someone has toward Janārdana, the god of gods,
just so much is his attainment of fruit; there is no doubt about this. / Whatever worship of Hari is performed without devotion by men on earth,
that worship, O best of brāhmaṇas, lasts only during the time of worship. / Devotion to Hari is rooted in knowledge; the worship of the lord of the world is rooted in devotion.
Worship is the root in the growth of the tree of liberation; adoration of Hari, / which a wise person performs with faith, even if very little,
all that becomes imperishable: every rite accompanied by faith. / He who worships Viṣṇu with devotion even with merely water, O twice-born,
obtains an abode in Viṣṇu's [realm], since Hari is subject to his devotee.
This whole world is worthless; only the worship of Hari is essential, O brāhmaṇa. / Therefore, a person desiring his own auspiciousness should sacrifice with devotion to Kṛṣṇa of boundless form.

7.12.m: Vyāsa said: / In Phālguna, O best of brāhmaṇas, a Vaiṣṇava person should worship / with devotional disposition glorious Kṛṣṇa, who is praised by the gods, every day.
He who bathes the son of Devakī with clarified butter in Phālguna, / I shall proclaim his fruit; listen to it properly.
Having obtained the fruit of all sacrifices, and likewise the fruit of all gifts, / free from all sins, he goes at the end to Hari's abode.
Having enjoyed enjoyment in Hari's house for thousands of tens of millions of yugas, / having attained the highest knowledge, he attains liberation right there.
He who offers a divine sesame sweetmeat to Kṛṣṇa in the cool season, / to him who has the form of a cowherd, goes to Hari's mansion.
He who gives milk-laḍḍus to great-souled Keśava / drinks nectar in heaven for the duration of a hundred manvantaras.
He who gives pleasant pieces [of candied sugar] to Hari, O Jaimini, / to him Viṣṇu, pleased in spirit, cuts off the bond of worldly existence.
He who gives varied, fruitful, divine [fruit] to the Blessed One, O twice-born, / having gone to Śakra's city at the end, becomes praised by the gods.
A devout person who gives pure sugar to Kṛṣṇa, / what does he not obtain, O brāhmaṇa, through the grace of Vāsudeva?
A fully ripe, sweet jujube fruit in the month of Phālguna— / he who offers it to Kṛṣṇa, listen to his fruit:
In this world he enjoys all happiness, accompanied by sons and grandsons; / at the end, having mounted a splendid chariot, he goes to Hari's house.
One should not give a jujube fruit mixed with raw sugar to Hari; / if one should give it out of ignorance, O best of brāhmaṇas, he becomes a dweller in hell.
In the month of Phālguna, he who gives a pomegranate fruit to Hari, / fully ripe, listen to that fruit as it is told by me, O brāhmaṇa:
As many seeds as remain in that pomegranate fruit, / for that many manvantaras does the fortunate one dwell in Viṣṇu's house.
He who gives a cake made with raw sugar to Hari in the month of Phālguna, / that best of the twice-born should be known as a performer of a thousand horse sacrifices.
In the month of Caitra, O best of the twice-born, if a mortal bathes / Madhusūdana with honey, he attains that supreme abode of Viṣṇu.
He who bathes Nārāyaṇa, the faultless one, with honey, / no investigation of him is ever made by the son of the Sun.
He who worships the lord of Kamalā with a kiṃśuka flower in Caitra, / his name is not written by Citragupta in the register.
In Caitra, for one who has worshipped Kṛṣṇa, the lord of the worlds, with tilaka flowers, / there is certainly no birth again on this surface of the earth.
A man worshipping the crest-jewel of all the gods with black vañjula flowers, / O brāhmaṇa, never meets with misfortune.
He who worships the Blessed One with fragrant vāsantī flowers in the spring, / pleased in spirit, is worshipped even by the gods.
Likewise, he who worships Hari with whole, divine sprouts, / rising even from his seated pedestal, he bows to him.
A person who worships Hari with fresh, tender myrobalan leaves / obtains everything desired without delay.
With unbroken leaves of wood-apple, with dhattūra flowers and arka flowers, / he who worships Viṣṇu and the Lord crosses to the other shore of the ocean of saṃsāra.
He who gives an excellent plantain fruit to Viṣṇu, O brāhmaṇa, / all the thirty gods, headed by Śakra, bow to him day and night.
He who in the month of Caitra gives wheat cake with devotion / to the one who takes the form of a cowherd, O brāhmaṇa, is released from all sins.
When the sacred month of Mādhava has arrived, beloved of Mādhava, / a devotee of Viṣṇu should renounce meat, sexual intercourse, and oil.
When the month of Mādhava arrives, a Vaiṣṇava should perform bathing; / he should abandon food belonging to another and should not eat twice [a day].
At dawn, he should worship Viṣṇu according to the rules mentioned before, O twice-born; / in Vaiśākha, he should bathe Viṣṇu with water scented with flowers.
He should bathe Acyuta in cool water until twilight; / with devotion he should worship the Lord at the three twilights with various food offerings.
Adorned in Vaiśākha with garlands of damana blossoms, / what would the Supreme Lord, the consort of Lakṣmī, pleased, not give, O brahmin sage?
He who offers barley food to the Discus-Holder in the month of Vaiśākha— / what wise man is capable of counting his merits?
Whatever is given in the month of Mādhava for the sake of pleasing Mādhava, / [given] to Mādhava alone, all that becomes inexhaustible.
Whatever other good deed is done in the month of Mādhava / for the pleasure of Mādhava, O brahmin, there is no destruction of it.
A person who sets up a water booth in the month of Vaiśākha to satisfy Mādhava / obtains the fruit of a horse sacrifice day after day.
Vaiśākha is a rare month, granting the fruit of all rites; / Hari should be worshipped during it, leaving aside even hundreds of rites.
Whatever fruit one obtains by worshipping Hari continually for six years, / one obtains even by performing worship of Hari for a single day in Vaiśākha.
A Vaiṣṇava person who daily [worships] Viṣṇu in the form of an aśvattha tree in the month of Vaiśākha, / for the sake of attaining the fruit of the four aims of life,
who renders service to an aśvattha tree even with a handful of water, / even he, freed from tens of millions of sins, goes to the supreme abode.
He who binds the root of an aśvattha with stones and other materials, O brahmin sage— / what does the Blessed Lord in the form of an aśvattha not give to him?
If, beholding an aśvattha tree, one bows down to it, / he too goes to the supreme abode; his life span increases, there is no doubt.
Whatever pious act a person performs beneath an aśvattha, O brahmin, / there is neither deficiency nor excess in that deed, O Jaimini.
All the sacred fords, beginning with the Tristrotas, are there, O Jaimini, / where even a single aśvattha tree, the best of trees, stands.
He who worships the aśvattha is indeed a worshipper of Viṣṇu, / because the Blessed Lord is Himself the embodiment of the aśvattha, O twice-born.
The foolish-minded one who, out of disrespect, cuts down an aśvattha, O best of the twice-born— / there is no deed in the world by performing which he may be purified.
This aśvattha, king of trees, is celebrated as the embodiment of Hari; / therefore, there is no protector for those who destroy an aśvattha.
For one who looks at the aśvattha, touches it, and furthermore, O brahmin, / for one who bows down, Hari removes every sin abiding in the body.
He who, having seen a destroyer of an aśvattha, does not prevent him although capable, / both of his eyes are plucked out by Yama himself with fishhooks.
He who does not say, 'Fool, do not cut the aśvattha,' / his tongue the King of the Dead cuts out himself with a knife.
He who destroys even a single small branch of an aśvattha, / that person obtains the fruit of ten million murders of a brahmin.
Whatever sin is in the murder of a brahmin, in going with a teacher's wife, / in drinking liquor, and likewise in theft, and also in misappropriating a deposit,
whatever sin is in killing an embryo, in killing a cow, O best of the twice-born, / and whatever sin is in killing a woman, and likewise in going with another's wife,
in killing one who has sought refuge, and likewise in killing a friend, / in speaking false words, and in the act of injuring one's husband,
whatever sin is in reviling others, and in eating on Hari's day— / all that terrible sin is incurred by people from cutting down an aśvattha.
The person who, out of delusion, cuts down an aśvattha, the embodiment of Viṣṇu— / no sinner equal to him has ever been heard of in the orb of the earth.
I shall declare the glorification of the aśvattha, which destroys all sins, / along with a legendary history, O best of the twice-born; listen with concentrated mind, dear child.
Formerly, in the Tretā age, there was a brahmin named Dhanañjaya, O twice-born, / devoted to Hari, delighting in the welfare of all living beings,
always devoted to honouring his kinsmen, ever intent on the gift of lamps, / speaking the truth, having conquered anger, free from violence and deceit.
That seeker of liberation, best of the twice-born, constantly worshipped / the Supreme Lord, the Lord Nārāyaṇa, with supreme devotion.
Then, knowing his great and very firm devotion, the Lord / took away all his wealth by some mere pretext.
Even so, that wise and best of the twice-born performed the worship / of the noble Keśava day after day with supreme devotion.
Having seen that the wealth acquired with suffering was all destroyed, O twice-born, / the brahmin was distressed, his mind troubled by sorrow.
That brahmin, knower of the highest truth, gave up eating, / firmly fixing his own mind upon the worship of Mahāviṣṇu.
Then Janārdana, who is steadfast and grants peace, knowing again the devotion / of that brahmin, brought about separation from his kinsmen.
The kinsmen of that brahmin, bewildered by the illusory power of Viṣṇu, / began to do injury [to him] constantly, O best of the twice-born.
Then the brahmin, freed and detached from kinsmen, continually worshipped / Puruṣottama, pleased and full of abundant devotion.
That earthly god, having dedicated his wealth to the worship of Keśava, / Mādhava, the Lord of the Universe, abandoned grief for his kinsmen.
Then again Mahāviṣṇu, fond of sport, O Jaimini, / although compassionate, took away his sons day after day.
Even so, that best of the twice-born daily worshipped Viṣṇu, / Keśava, the destroyer of suffering, with devotion twice as great as before.
Then his wife, O brahmin, deeply afflicted by pain and sorrow, / went to her father's house, completely bewildered by the illusory power of Viṣṇu.
Then that earthly god, alone, devoted to devotion to Viṣṇu, / never thought of misfortune in his virtuous mind.
Once, that best of the twice-born, foremost of those who possess devotion to Viṣṇu, / placing an axe on his shoulder, went to the forest for wood.
Bringing wood from the forest, that twice-born every day, / lacking clothes at the onset of winter, kept off the cold.
Once, unable to go to the forest, the best of the twice-born / struck a branch of an aśvattha tree standing in his courtyard.
At that moment, Mahāviṣṇu, the foremost of the gods, his mind distressed with pain, / came forth from that aśvattha tree.

The brahmin saw Viṣṇu before him, four-armed, with eyes wide like lotus petals, / wearing yellow garments, adorned with earrings, with beautiful hair, bearing His own weapons beginning with the lotus,

His broad stream of trickling blood like a fresh cloud made crimson in the twilight, / looking like the sun, yet pleasant, the Supreme Lord who cannot be seen by the hosts of gods; / both his eyes charming with streams of tears of joy, the brahmin praised [Him] with gentle words.
The brahmin said: / 'O Hari, Murāri, Sole Lord of the Universe, Govinda, Dāmodara, Mādhava, / Consort of Lakṣmī, Keśava, Foe of Keśin, Nārāyaṇa, Infinite One, All-pervading Lord, be gracious!'

What can I say of your incarnation? Without you, nothing exists here on earth. / Or what [can I say] of your qualities that pervade the whole universe, or of your compassion that treats friend and foe as one?
Bestowing one's own devotion unto someone, O Lord Viṣṇu, unto Hari whose form is imperishable— / 'Receiving prosperity, I shall bestow delight'—devotion bestowed upon the great is most blessed.
I constantly consider myself, O one of endless forms, as the foremost of sinners; / for that very reason, a sinner does not behold your pair of feet, which are worthy of divine contemplation.
Although I consider myself the most afflicted among the sorrowful, today, O Viṣṇu, / I look upon myself as Indra, since with my own two eyes I directly behold you, the Soul of the universe.
I know not even the slightest worship of you, nor do I ever offer wealth to you; / nevertheless, you have appeared embodied before me—you, Keśava, the sole object of worship, have been seen by me.

This tree of devotion to me was granted by you, yielding only the triad of dharma, wealth, and desire; / sprinkled today by the rain-shower of your sight, O Lord, it has borne the fruit of final liberation.
May my head become the foremost of all heads in the world before Keśava, who possesses the universal form; / indeed, my mind now goes to your pair of lotus feet, O God of gods!
Vyāsa said: / Having praised Nārāyaṇa, the Lord of the universe, who is free from affliction, / that virtuous twice-born one with folded hands spoke to him again with devotion:
The brāhmaṇa said: / O God of gods, O Lord of the universe, cause of grace to the world! / By blows of an axe, this body of yours has been bathed in blood.
The races of all the Daityas have been destroyed by you in battle; / who on earth is capable of striking you? O Lord, this is a great wonder!
The Blessed One said: / My child, what you have spoken is true; there is no doubt about this. / No Dānava or Rākṣasa is capable of striking me.
I myself, in the form of the sacred fig tree, was struck by you with an axe; / therefore, O twice-born, a flow of blood has now arisen in my body.
Vyāsa said: / Hearing this word of his, that twice-born, overwhelmed with fear, / condemned himself in many ways through his own mind:
'Cursed indeed is that fortune of mine, the foremost among all sinners, / who has caused great pain in the heart of the Lord of the three worlds!
Viṣṇu, who removes all sins, has been afflicted by me. / It is not possible for me alone to cross over this sin.
When he is pleased, even sinners become revered by the gods; / he has been pained by the pain inflicted by me—alas, I am undone!
Whom the gods headed by Brahmā propitiate with intense devotion— / oh, pain has been given in his heart by a sinful one like me!
What use are austerities, what use are recitations, what use are homes or my life? / This sole giver of dharma, wealth, desire, and liberation has been afflicted with pain!'
Having spoken thus, that best of the twice-born resolved to strike / his own neck with that very axe for the sake of pleasing Viṣṇu.
Recognizing his steadfast devotion, the compassionate Lord of Kamalā, / fond of his devotees, swiftly took away that axe from his hand.
The Blessed Lord said: / Why, my child, do you perform such an exceedingly dreadful deed? / I am never pleased with men who commit suicide.
I am indeed pleased with your devotion; do not fear, O best of men! / Choose a boon, O chief of brāhmaṇas, whatever is in your heart.
The brāhmaṇa said: / This great pain has been inflicted by me, O Supreme Lord; / may it not remain in your body—this is the boon I ask, O Lord!
The Blessed Lord said: / My child, this act was done by you out of ignorance, O twice-born; / therefore, your offense is not to be regarded as great.
I must always protect you, since you are the foremost devotee; / I take upon myself your faults day after day, my child.
Even so, your great devotion to me has ever increased; / therefore, my child, I now desire to be free from debt to you.
Abandoning all fear, choose a boon before me. / The brāhmaṇa said: In you, the foremost of all gods, birth after birth,
let there be very firm devotion, O Hari! What need is there of other boons? / Vyāsa said: Hearing this speech of his, spoken out of love, Keśava,
being pleased, then gave him the garland resting on his own neck. / Then, embracing the brāhmaṇa with his four long arms like a father embracing a son,
the Lord spoke tender words: / The Blessed Lord said: Since you are my devotee, O twice-born, by my grace,
every auspiciousness will come to pass for you without delay, O twice-born! / Constantly worship me in the form of the sacred fig tree through practical yoga, O best of men;
I will fulfill all your desires. / Having spoken thus to that foremost twice-born and embraced him once again, Keśava,
the abode of compassion, suddenly disappeared right there. / Having obtained the garland from Viṣṇu's neck, that twice-born, the best of Vaiṣṇavas,
considered himself fulfilled and remained in his own home. / Then, O brāhmaṇa sage, by the command of Keśava, Kubera himself
showered abundant riches in the house of that brāhmaṇa. / A palace was constructed for him by the architect Viśvakarman,
by order of Nārāyaṇa, superior like Vaijayanta itself, / equipped with male and female servants, adorned with various articles,
filled with crores of elephants and horses; his mansion shone brightly. / His kinsmen, even those long lost, came and reunited with him.
His wife, who had shown him disrespect, returned to his house of her own accord. / Even his wife whose children had died, through the compassion of Keśava,
came to have living offspring, O twice-born, and became devoted in service to her husband. / Having long enjoyed all pleasures accompanied by sons and grandsons,
at the end of his life, that best of brāhmaṇas attained liberation along with his wife. / Vyāsa said: The sacred fig tree itself, the best of trees, is visibly Viṣṇu himself;
for men who practice devotion to it, no misfortune ever exists anywhere. / But whoever, having meditated upon Viṣṇu, attends upon the sacred fig tree, O best of men—
the Lord, being pleased, grants him the supreme abode.
